findings.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145 — Dropping the first hostname label incorrectly treats unrelated domains such as community.co.uk and unrelated.co.uk as the same domain, causing the full path to be shown. Compare registrable domains using public-suffix rules.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140 — Case-sensitive hostname comparisons incorrectly return EXAMPLE.com without the required path for website https://EXAMPLE.com/user on instance example.com. Normalize hostname case before comparing.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145 — Dropping the first hostname label incorrectly treats unrelated domains such as community.co.uk and unrelated.co.uk as the same domain, causing the full path to be shown. Compare registrable domains using public-suffix rules.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the domain comparison logic at line 145. The code `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` compares domains by dropping the first label, which would incorrectly treat 'community.co.uk' and 'unrelated.co.uk' as matching (both become 'co.uk'). This is a real defect in the logic that could cause incorrect behavior for domains with country-code TLDs or other multi-part suffixes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140 — Case-sensitive hostname comparisons incorrectly return EXAMPLE.com without the required path for website https://EXAMPLE.com/user on instance example.com. Normalize hostname case before comparing.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the hostname comparisons in website_name method are case-sensitive. Looking at the diff, line 140 shows `website_host == discourse_host` and subsequent comparisons use direct string equality. URI hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC, so 'EXAMPLE.com' should match 'example.com', but Ruby string comparison is case-sensitive. This would cause the method to return just 'EXAMPLE.com' instead of 'EXAMPLE.com/user' when the hostnames differ only in case. The code should use downcase on both hostnames before comparing.
